subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw ship a narrow builtin memorySearch.excludePaths contract now, or wait for a shared cross-backend recall/index path-scope contract?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the permanent API affects public config, memory recall semantics, QMD parity, diagnostics, and indexed memory state.

options.title: Ship narrow exclusion first
options.body: Repair and accept a builtin-only excludePaths contract with explicit docs, while tracking QMD/path-drift diagnostics as follow-up work.

options.title: Require shared path scopes
options.body: Hold the fix until builtin indexing, QMD collections, recall eligibility, watcher behavior, and diagnostics share one include/exclude model.

options.title: Do docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and focus on path-drift, broad-extraPaths, and benchmark-contamination guidance plus stronger status warnings.

recommendation.title: Ship narrow exclusion first
recommendation.body: Repair and accept a builtin-only excludePaths contract with explicit docs, while tracking QMD/path-drift diagnostics as follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history strongest links vincentkoc to memory config, host SDK cleanup, QMD extraPaths merge decisions, and the docs/config boundary.
